questions.question: A posture check needs joint positions, not boxes or labels. What output shape gives that?
questions.explanation: Joints are points, not regions. This lesson locates keypoints through heatmap peaks.

questions.question: What output shape does TinyKeypointNet produce for input (N,3,64,64) with num_keypoints=4?
questions.explanation: Two stride-2 convolutions reduce the map to 16x16 and two stride-2 transposed convolutions restore 64x64, with four heatmap channels.

questions.question: For a heatmap with width W, how does heatmap_to_coords convert a flattened argmax index idx to x?
questions.explanation: The remainder after division by width is the column coordinate; integer division gives the row y.

questions.question: What does the training loss in the demo compare?
options: Argmax coordinates and class IDs with cross-entropy
The input image and a random pose sequence
Predicted keypoint heatmaps and Gaussian target heatmaps with MSE
questions.explanation: The model output is resized to the target heatmap size and optimized with F.mse_loss(pred,hms).

questions.question: When does subpixel_refine adjust an argmax coordinate?
options: Only when the peak is not on the heatmap border, using neighboring values
Only when the heatmap has no maximum
By replacing every coordinate with the image center
It never reads neighboring heatmap pixels
questions.explanation: The helper checks 0<x<W-1 and 0<y<H-1, then uses finite differences around the peak to make a small refinement.

questions.question: What does a bottom-up pose pipeline need beyond independent keypoint heatmaps?
options: A single image-level class label with no coordinates
An association step such as Part Affinity Fields to group keypoints into person instances
Only a larger RGB color palette
A second OCR decoder for each heatmap
questions.explanation: Bottom-up methods detect all joints first and then associate them into people; PAFs are one way to encode limb connectivity.
